message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes of all time. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high‑school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he was named the 2003 Mr. Basketball America and led his team to a state championship.

He entered the NBA directly from high school, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers in the 2003 draft. LeBron quickly became known for his combination of size, athleticism, passing ability, and basketball IQ. He has played for the Cleveland Cavaliers (2003–2010, 2014–2018), Miami Heat (2010–2014), and Los Angeles Lakers (2018–present). His accolades include:

* 4× NBA Most Valuable Player (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013)
* 4× NBA Finals MVP (2012, 2013, 2016, 2020)
* 17× NBA All‑Star (2005–2021)
* 2× Olympic gold medalist (2008, 2012)
* NBA champion with Miami Heat (2012, 2013) and Cleveland Cavaliers (2016)

Beyond the court, LeBron is also a philanthropist, entrepreneur, and media personality. He founded the LeBron James Family Foundation, which opened the “I Promise” school in Akron to support at‑risk youth. He has produced and starred in films and television shows, including the critically acclaimed “Space Jam: A New Legacy” (2021) and the HBO series “The Shop.” LeBron’s influence extends into business ventures such as his partnership with Nike, his production company SpringHill Entertainment, and his ownership stake in the Los Angeles Dodgers baseball franchise.
